When the handle is shaken, the threaded shaft can force the two arms of the jack to move closer together, thereby jacking up the car. When the wheel has just been jacked up, the pressure of the car on the jack is $1.0\times10^5N$, and at this time the angle between the two arms of the jack is $120^{\circ}$. Which of the following judgments is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: If the handle continues to be shaken to jack up the car, the pressure on each arm of the jack will decrease

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, a jack commonly used for cars, when the handle is shaken, the threaded shaft can force the two arms of the jack to move closer together, thereby jacking up the car. When the wheel has just been jacked up, the pressure of the car on the jack is $1.0\times10^5\text{ N}$, and at this time the angle between the two arms of the jack is $120^{\circ}$. If the handle continues to be shaken to jack up the car, how will the pressure on each arm of the jack change?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: If the handle continues to be shaken to jack up the car, the pressure on each arm of the jack will decrease
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is the side of a car, and the wheel can be seen on the left side; below the car body is placed a scissor jack, the jack supports the car body with inclined support arms, and on the right side is connected a handle/crank. Shaking it can change the distance between the support arms through the threaded shaft. Then reason: The problem statement gives that when the wheel has just been jacked up, the pressure of the car on the jack is P=1.0×10^5 N, and at this time the angle between the two arms of the jack is θ=120°. Regard the two arms of the jack as symmetric compression rods, and let the pressure on each arm be F. The vertical components of the two arms together support the car's pressure, therefore P=2F cos(θ/2). When the handle continues to be shaken, the threaded shaft forces the two arms to move closer together, and the included angle θ becomes smaller; thus θ/2 becomes smaller, and cos(θ/2) becomes larger. Under the condition that P is approximately unchanged, F=P/[2cos(θ/2)] therefore becomes smaller. So the pressure on each arm decreases.
